claim: AP-4 recognises a tyrosine signal in the ATG9A N-terminal cytosolic region
finding: ATG9A identified as a specific AP-4 cargo; signal-mediated TGN export; Ala scan Y8A/Q9A/L11A/E12A abolish AP-4 binding, R10A and Y15A do not; UniProt curates motif 8-11 (ECO:0000269) and a reciprocal AP4M1-ATG9A IPI
context: human cell lines; AP4E1/AP4B1 KO; binding assays
confidence: high for motif identity; full text not in PMC OA so assay format and mu4 site not verifiable here

claim: ATG9A is an AP-4 cargo in diverse cells
finding: Dynamic Organellar Maps identify ATG9A, SERINC1, SERINC3 as AP-4-dependent cargo; ATG9A missorted in patient-derived cells

claim: AP4M1 loss causes ATG9A TGN retention
finding: 15 patient fibroblast lines incl. AP4M1/SPG50 and 6 iPSC-neuron lines: ATG9A accumulates at TGN, 3-5x protein increase, rescued by subunit re-expression; autophagic flux intact in fibroblasts
context: human primary fibroblasts, iPSC cortical neurons
confidence: high for mislocalisation; autophagy effect cell-type dependent

claim: mu4 has a noncanonical CTD site that reads APP YKFFE
finding: YKFFE binds mu4 at a site distinct from other signal-adaptor interactions; PDB 3L81. Contact analysis here: F690 buries 91 atom pairs in a pocket closed by R283
confidence: high for APP; extension to ATG9A is inference

claim: Which mu4 site is energetically required
finding: R283D at the noncanonical site abolishes APP binding; D190A at the canonical site reduces affinity; mu subunits retain a canonical YxxO site via a critical Asp
confidence: high; tested only with the APP signal, never with ATG9A

citation: this work (UniProt Q7Z3C6 topology + regex scan)
claim: YQRLE is the best candidate motif
finding: Across all 653 cytosolic residues: 6 YxxO, 1 acidic dileucine, and exactly one Yxx[bulky][DE] = YQRLE 8-12, the only candidate in a disordered region

claim: Motif should be absent where AP-4 is absent
finding: YQRLE at position 8 in 7/7 vertebrate ATG9A; absent in Drosophila, C. elegans, Arabidopsis, S. cerevisiae, S. pombe ATG9, all of which lack all four AP-4 subunits (Fisher p=0.0013)
confidence: moderate-high; gene-name-based ortholog search, not phylogenomics

claim: The motif is the general AP-4 recognition code
finding: SERINC1/3/5 cytosolic domains contain zero YxxO and zero Yxx[bulky][DE] motifs

claim: The motif matches the noncanonical aromatic APP-type signal
finding: ATG9A YQRLE shares the identical YQRL tetrapeptide and an acidic +4 with TGN46/TGOLN2 YQRLD, the archetypal canonical YxxO signal; ATG9A has Leu, not an aromatic, at the +3 pocket position
confidence: moderate; sequence similarity does not fix binding site

claim: ATG9A uses the noncanonical R283 site
finding: R283 is Gln in Xenopus and zebrafish mu4 while ATG9A YQRLE is invariant in those species; canonical D190 is invariant in mu1A, mu2, mu3A and all mu4 orthologs
confidence: moderate; R283Q never tested, Gln retains H-bonding capacity

claim: Motif presence explains ATG9A-specific cargo selection
finding: ATG9B retains a mammal-conserved positional equivalent YERLE (human 151, mouse 150, rat 150, cow YEQLE 151), differing only at the +1 position that is essential in ATG9A
confidence: moderate; positional equivalence anchored on a 53%-identity block, linker not alignable

finding: Review states AP-4 recognises cargos having specific sorting signals in their cytosolic domains; cargos are APP, ATG9A, SERINC3/5
